description: This line plot, titled “AGNews, clean-label, poison_rate: 10% (2.5% of total),” illustrates the attack success rate (ASR) across eight different target classes—cf, bb, WNBA, ESPN, NHL, FIFA, Estadio, and athletics—under three trigger insertion strategies: “start” (teal line with circle markers), “random” (orange line with cross markers), and “end” (purple line with circle markers). The x-axis lists the target classes in categorical order without a numerical scale, while the y-axis represents ASR on a linear scale ranging from 0.5 to 0.9, with tick marks at 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9. The “start” strategy begins at ASR ≈ 0.77 for “cf,” drops sharply to ≈ 0.49 for “bb,” rises to ≈ 0.90 for “WNBA,” fluctuates between ≈ 0.82 and 0.92 across subsequent classes, and ends at ≈ 0.92 for “athletics.” The “random” strategy starts at ≈ 0.65 for “cf,” dips to ≈ 0.51 for “bb,” peaks at ≈ 0.89 for “WNBA,” declines to ≈ 0.72 for “ESPN,” then rises again to ≈ 0.92 for “Estadio” before falling to ≈ 0.86 for “athletics.” The “end” strategy begins at ≈ 0.75 for “cf,” drops to ≈ 0.57 for “bb,” climbs to ≈ 0.89 for “WNBA,” dips to ≈ 0.75 for “ESPN,” peaks at ≈ 0.89 for “NHL,” falls to ≈ 0.81 for “FIFA,” surges to ≈ 0.96 for “Estadio,” and ends at ≈ 0.83 for “athletics.” All three lines exhibit significant variation across classes, with “end” achieving the highest peak ASR (≈ 0.96) and “start” showing the most consistent high performance toward the end of the x-axis.
